FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finahzed by the Cement Matnx Products Secnonal Committee had been approved by the CIvil Engmeenng DIVISion Council ThISstandard was published In 1959 and subsequently revised In 1978 to Introduce prestressed concrete cylinder pipes. requirements of fittings, provision of more details on design cntena for the pipes, etc This standard lays down the requirements of prestressed concrete pipes pnmanly used for the conveyance of water and sewerage and specials for use Withthem Two types of prestressed concrete pipes are covered by this spccificanon, namely, prestressed concrete cyhnder pipes and prestressed concrete non-cylinder pipes

Thrs second revrsion Incorporates number of modifications, the most Significant of them bemg
a) b) c) d) modifications 10 design and other aspects, mclusion of typical worked out examples of design, mclusion of detailed inspection procedure, and Increase In range of diameters of pipes

In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been derived for EN 642 1994 Prestressed Concrete Pressure PIpes, Cylinder and Non-Cylinder, European Committee for Standardization (CEN) The composition of the technical committee responsible for formulation of this standard

1 SCOPE
ThIS standard covers the requirements of prestressed concrete pipes (including specials) with nominal internal diameter 10 the range of 200 mm to 2 500 mm (see Note under Table 1), in which permanent Internal stresses are dehberately Introduced by tensioned steel to the desired degree to counteract the stresses caused m pipe under service
2 REFERENCES

3.5 Site Test Pressure - I 5 times working pressure pertammg to the section or I I times static pressure, whichever IS more (surge pressure IS to be controlled withm 25 percent of pump head m case of pumping main)

3.6 Factory Test Pressure
a) Site test pressure b) SIte test pressure pressure + 0 I N/mm 2, for working upto 1 N/mm2, and pressure + 0 2 Nzrnrrr', for working above 1 N/mm 2

3.7 Surge (Water Hammer) Pressure It IS a pressure which IS produced by a change of velocity ofthe moving stream and becomes maximum when there IS sudden stoppage which may be caused by the closmg of a valve or by shuttmg down a pump station Surge pressure IS to be controlled withm 25 percent of pump head 4 MATERIALS 4.1 Cement The cement used 10 the manufacture of prestressed concrete pipes and specials shall be one of the following a) 43 grade ordinary Portland cement confomung to IS 8112 b) 53 grade ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 12269 c) Rapid harden 109 Portland cement conforming to IS 8041 d) Portland slag cement conformmg to IS 455 With slag not more than 50 percent e) Sulphate resisting Portland cement conforming to IS 12330

stressed and coated With cement mortar or concrete to protect the circumferential prestressing Wife, to Withstand internal pressure and external design loads 3.3 Specials - All Items In the pipeline other than straight pipes of standard length, such as bends, air valves and scour valve tees, etc, are classified as

8 MANUFACTURE
8.1 Core
8.1.1 Moulds The moulds and method of manufacture of pipe shall be such that the form and dimensions of the finished pipe conform to the requirements given 10 Sand 12 and the surface and edges are clean and true 8.1.2 Concrete M,x The proportions of cement, fine aggregate, coarse aggregate and water used 10 concrete for pipe core shall be determined and controlled as the work proceeds to obtam homogenous, dense, workable, durable concrete

8.3 Pretensioning and Release of Longitudinal Wires
The concrete core shall be longitudinally prestressed, mcluding the socket, by means of high tens lie steel wires or strands, which shall be provided With permanent anchorages embedded In the concrete, Within the joint portion at each end The centrehne spacing between the longitudinal wires measured along the barrel shall not exceed twice the core thickness or 150 mm, whichever IS greater, subject to the provision of 7.4.1(c) The clear cover ofconcrete over all steel reinforcement Including the ends of the longrtudmal prestressing WIres, shall be such that In any finished pipe It IS nowhere less than 12 mm

of specified strength m the pipe, and mmunurn defects
011 the surface of the pipe The proportions shall be those, that Will give the best overall results With the particular matenals and the methods of placmg used for the work A minimum of350 kg/m! ofcement shall be used for concrete The water cement ratio shall be such, as to ensure that the concrete WIllmeet the strength requirements, but in no case It shall exceed 0 5 The soluble chloride Ion content of the concrete or mortar mix, expressed as a percentage of the mass of cement shall not exceed 0 20 percent

8.3.1 The longitudmal wires shall be stressed to the
designed tension, taking into account the loss of stress In wire The tension shall be mamtamed by posinve means nll detensionmg

IS 784 : 2001 8.4.2 The Initial stress In the wire dunng circumferential wmding shall not be more than 7S percent of'the muumum ultimate tensile strength ofWIre,when counter-weight or break system IS used for developmg tension If tension IS developed by use of a die, then the miual stress In the wire shall not exceed 6S percent of the ultimate tensile strength of wire 8.4.3 The uunal compressive stressinduced 10 the core concrete shall not exceed SS percent of the compressive strength of the concrete 10 the pipe at the tune oftransfer 8.4.4 Methods and equipments for wrapping the wire shall be such that wire shall be wound around the core m a hehcal form at the predetermined design spacing anti capable of controlling the tension Wire sphcmg shall be capable of withstanding a force equal to the fuJI strength of wife At the ends of core pipe, the wire shall continue for at least one extra circurnferennal turn before being anchored

8.5.3 Pneumatic process In which mixing of mgredients IS camed out at the nozzle or gun, shall not be pemutted 8.5.4 The compressive strength of the cover coating mortar shall be obtained from cubes having area of face SO cm 2 or the compressive strength of the cover coanng concrete shall be obtained from cube having area of face 100 cm 2 and shall not be less than 3S N/mm 2 at the time of factory testing of pipe 8.5.5 The mortar coating shall have a mmimum cover of 18 mm and concrete coating shall have a rmmmum cover of 25 mm, over all steel, except at end face and the spigot portion going mside socket, where It Will be not less than IS mm To achieve adequate bond between core and coat, approved bonding agent shall be apphed, at ends of pipe for a Width of 100 mm, along the circumference to prevent separation between core and coat, at ends
Concurrently With the mortar coatmg, a cement slurry shall be applted on to the core at a rate of not less than 05 Vm2 Just ahead of the mortar coating The slurry shall consist of 1 2 kg of cement to per htre of water

8.4.6 Test Cube Conversion Factors
The core concrete compressive strength shall be taken on 150 mm x 1SO mm cubes Where the process of manufacture I~ such that the strength of concrete 10 the pipe differs from that given by tests on VIbrated cubes, the two may be related by suitable conversion factors If the purchaser requires evidence of these factors, he shall ask for It, before placing the order The core concrete strength shall be obtained by multiplymg the cube strength with the conversion tactor and shall be used for design purpose

8.5.6 The thickness shall be checked for every pipe as soon as, coating IS done

8.5.7 Mortar Soundness
After the mortar coating IScured and prior to transport, the coating on each pipe shall be checked for delammation and hollows by tapping the extenor WIth a hammer having a head mass of not more than o 5 kg Any hollows or drumrmng areas detected by sounding shall be repaired by approved methods

8.5 Cover Coating 8.5.1 The circumferential prestressing wires on the core pipes shall be protected Witha layerofnch cement mortar or concrete or any other approved material which prevents corrosion of wife 8.5.2 I f cement mortar IS used for cover coating, It shall be apphed by rotary brushes or by other approved methods and shall preferably be apphed Within 16 hours after the prestressing wire ISwound The cement, sand and water shall be thoroughly mixed, before being fed mto the cover coating mach me Mmimum cement content m coating mortar shall be 540 kg/m' and that for concrete 500 kg/m! Water cement ratio In the mix shall not be less than 027, If cement mortar IS used for COdling Rebound or droppings not exceeding one fourth of the total mass of mix, may be used but the resulting mix proportions shall not be, leaner than origmal design mix Rebound not used Within one hour, shall be discarded 6

8.5.8 All cement coming In contact WIth each other shall be of same type and composition and shall be from the same cement works 9 ADDITIONAL CYLINDER PIPES REQUIREMENTS FOR

9.1 The prestressed concrete cyhnder pipes shall be manufactured to comply Withthe following additional requirements

9.1.1 Steel Socket and SpIgot Rmgs
Each nng shall be formed by one piece of steel or a number of pieces of steel butt-welded together The rings shall be expanded beyond their elastic hmit so that they are accurately shaped The portion of the socket and spigot nngs which shall be exposed after the pipe IScompleted shall besmooth to prevent cuttmg of the rubber gasket dunng jomtmg and shall be protected from corrosion by a sprayed zinc coating of rmrumum thickness of 0 OS mm followed by one coat of bitummous paint Other SUItableprotection may be used WIth the approval of the purchaser

IS 784 : 2001 9.1.2 Fabrication ofSteel Cylmders The cyhnder shall be accurately shaped to the size required and steel socket and spigot nngs welded thereto after being Jigged square with the longitudinal axis (except for bevel) 9.1.2.1 Testing Before It IS subjected to any further manufactunng process, each steel cyhnder, with steel and spigot nngs welded on, shall be subjected to water pressure which stresses the steel to at least 140 Nzmnr', but not more than 175 N/mm 2 While under stress, the assembly especially welds, shall be Inspected and any parts showing leakage shall be repaired and the whole assembly retested 10 SPECIALS 10.1 Fabrication
The steel for fabricated steel plate specials, IS cut, shaped and welded so that the finished special has the required shape and Internal dimensions Adjacent segments are jointed by butt welding Before lmmg and coat 109, the welding of specials shall be tested by use of hot Oil or dye penetrant according to IS 3658 and defects, If any shall be rectified The steel plate thickness for specials shall be as given 10 IS 1916 In die penetratton test, a white wash IS apphed over the weld on one Side of the cyhnder, on other Side when coloured paraffin or Similar product IS apphed over the weld, no coloured spot shall appear on the whitewash before 4 h If any coloured spots appear before 4 h, weld shall be repaired and retested seahng nng, the JOint shall be self centremg, flexible and water tight The JOint shall be roll-on or confined type Sockets of the pipes may be projecting or flush With the barrel JOint design shall be furnished by manufacturer before undertaking manufacture The rubber nng JOint design, shall take into consideration the tolerance for rubber chord, tolerance for socket and spigot diameters, allowable deflection at J010tand permanent set 10 the rubber nng

11.2 The seahng nngs shall be of such SIZC that when jointed, 10 accordance Withthe manufacturer's mstrucnons, It shall provide a POSitiveseal withm the manufacturer's recommended range of maximum joint deflection Not more than two sphces 10each nng shall be permitted 12 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 12.1 Deviation from the Straightness
When measured by means of a one metre straight edge the devianon from straight per metre length shall not exceed 5 mm

12.2 Finish
Pipe shall be free from local depressions or bulges greater than 5 mm extending over a length, 10 any direction, greater than twice the thickness of barrel The external surface of the pipe may be sand faced, when coating of cement mortar IS apphed

13 TEST 13.1 Design Proving and Manufacturing Process Approval Test in Factory
As soon as 4 to 5 pipes are made, these shall be 10stalled and sue pressure test shall be conducted, to prove and finahze pipe and joint design and joint dimension tolerances, etc For one diameter and different pressure, only the test for highest pressure shall be done For this test no external load shall apphed

10.2 Lining and Coating Steel plate specials are hned and coated Withconcrete or cement mortar or other approved matenals, as agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser The proportion of cement to total aggregate shall not be leaner than 1 3 by mass 10.3 Reinforcement
For concrete or cement mortar coating, reinforcement shall be SUitably tack welded to the shell The reinforcement shall be wife rods and spirals or wire mesh or wire fabnc

13.2 Hydrostatic Factory Test
The pipe shall be tested In accordance With IS 3597 The pipe must not show leakage Damp or wet patches shall be accepted If the pipe falls to pass the test, It can be cured or repaired to Improve Its water tightness and then retested In case the pipe does not stand the rated mternal pressure, It shall be accepted for lower pressure, purchaser at his own discretion may accept the pipes for lower pressure to which It WIthstands, provided all other requirements are conforming to this standard Non-pressure pipes for drainage, sewerage and culverts, shall be tested for 0 14 N/mm 2 7

10.4 Jointing Between Special and Pipe
The special shall be jointed to the pipe by same rubber rangJOint as for pipes or by caulking With mortar For this purpose steel collars shall be welded to steel specials to allow caulking of JOint With mortar This ISallowed only upto working pressure of 3 kglcm 2

11 JOINTS 11.1 Unless specified otherwise, joints between pipes shall be of the spigot and socket type, so manufactured, that when fitted With the correct size rubber

BIS IS a statutory Institution estabhshed under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quahty certification of goods and attending to connected matters In the country

Copyright
BIS has the copyright of all Its pubhcanons No part of these pubhcanons may be reproduced In any form without the prior permission In wntmg of BIS This does not preclude the free use, In the course of Implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and Sizes, type or grade designanons l-nqumes relating to copyright be addressed to the DIrector (Pubhcanons), BIS

Review of Indlan Standards
Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the baSISof comments Standards are also reviewed periodically, a standard along with amendments IS reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed, If the review mdicates that changes are needed, It IS taken up for revision Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are m possession of the latest amendments or edition by refernng to the latest Issue of BIS Catalogue' and 'Standards Monthly Addinons'
